<details>
<summary>How to take this update (instructions for Claude)</summary>

This pull request raises locked dependencies to fix security advisories. **It is not merged on GitHub**: `vendor/` and the built UI bundles are committed, so a raw lockfile bump leaves them stale. A composer bump therefore fails `Run tests` at `make check-vendor-matches-lock` by design, and a UI bump fails it at `make check-ui-bundles` when the built bundle changes. The update is reproduced locally in a pull request of our own. Take it in this order: decide for each package whether the update can change something our application relies on and whether a test would notice, add the missing tests first, then reproduce the update, run the checks and open our pull request.

1. Read the tables and the `jsonl` blocks below, one JSON object per line. A package with `fixes` is the reason for this pull request; one without was pulled in by the resolver, and for PHP `required_by` says by whom. Look hardest at:
   - `"jump": "major"` and `"minor"`; `"deduplicated"` and `"duplicated"` mean the lockfile now holds fewer or more versions of the package (whoever used the dropped version now gets `to`); `"reference"` is the same version from a newer commit.
   - `patches`: a composer-patches patch (`patches/`) on that package, which has to still apply to the new version.
   - `requires`: what the new version needs that the old one did not (including the PHP version), or no longer needs.
   - `constraint` and `constraint_was`: the `composer.json` or `ui/package.json` range of a direct dependency, and the one before this pull request. A changed range means the manifest is edited too: mention it in our pull request.
   - Lines `{"companions":[[package, from, to, jump], ...]}` hold the resolver-only packages of a large update in short form.
2. Fetch the change between the two versions.
   - PHP: `repository` with `from_ref` and `to_ref` (GitHub: `<repository>/compare/<from_ref>...<to_ref>`); clone it and `git diff <from_ref> <to_ref>`, and read the CHANGELOG, UPGRADE files and release notes in between. `composer show <package>` and `composer why <package>` give more.
   - JS: `npm diff --diff=<package>@<from> --diff=<package>@<to>`; read the package's changelog.
3. See what we use. `used_in` counts the files per top-level directory (`model`, `web`, `admin`, `symfony`, `tests`, … for PHP; for JS the project directory and the first directory below it, such as `ui/src`) that mention the package's `namespaces` (PHP) or its name in quotes, with or without a subpath (JS). It is a grep hint, and a missing `tests` entry does not prove a gap. `"no_namespaces": true` marks a package that autoloads only classes or files (for example `setasign/tfpdf`, `dg/mysql-dump`, `dg/ftp-deployment`): it has no `used_in` at all, so search for its class names yourself. Search for the classes, services, config keys and imports the diff touches yourself, across `model/`, `web/`, `admin/` and `symfony/`.
4. Give each package one verdict.
   - `NOT_AFFECTED`: nothing we use has changed.
   - `AFFECTED_AND_COVERED`: we use changed behaviour; name the test that would fail.
   - `AFFECTED_NOT_COVERED`: we use changed behaviour and no test would notice.
5. For every `AFFECTED_NOT_COVERED`, write the missing test first, in a separate pull request off `main`; it must pass on the old versions. Merge that first.
6. Reproduce the update on a branch off `main`, one pull request per ecosystem and all open Dependabot pull requests of that ecosystem together (composer and UI never in one, so a revert stays possible and the built files cannot conflict):
   - PHP (`composer.lock`): `git fetch origin pull/<this number>/head && git cherry-pick FETCH_HEAD`, then `./bin-docker/composer install --no-interaction`. `git status` must show only `vendor/<updated package>/…`, `vendor/composer/installed.json` and `installed.php`, plus `autoload_*` when a package's file list changed. Revert anything else with `git checkout -- <path>`; the root block of `installed.php` stays as committed. A patch that no longer applies fails the install. Commit the `vendor/` changes as a second commit, `Sync vendor/ with composer.lock`. Run `make check-vendor-matches-lock`, `make check-dockerignore`, `make tests-be` and `make phpstan`.
   - UI (`ui/yarn.lock`): cherry-pick the same way, then `make ui-deps`, `./bin-docker/yarn build`, `make test-ui` and `make check-ui-bundles`. When `web/soubory/ui` and `admin/files/ui` (`bundle.js`, `style.css`) change, they go into the SAME commit as the library change. When they do not change, the bundle is unchanged: say so in the pull request.
7. Open our pull request as ready (not a draft), name this one in it, and wait for a green `Run tests`; a green run only shows that the existing tests pass, it says nothing about behaviour no test covers. Then hand ours over for review: a person merges it. Dependabot closes this pull request once the bump is on `main`. Never merge, approve or rebase this one, and never push to its branch.
</details>
